The operation validates that the parent section exists and is active before processing the image upload. It supports various image formats including JPEG, PNG, and GIF with comprehensive metadata storage including file dimensions, size, and accessibility information.

operations.description:
Create a new article in the discussion board platform.

This operation allows authenticated members to publish articles within designated sections of the discussion board. When creating an article, users must provide a title meeting length requirements (5-200 characters), substantive content (minimum 50 characters), and select a valid section for publication. The system automatically assigns the author based on the authenticated user context and generates server-managed fields including unique identifier, creation timestamp, and initial publication status.

Articles are created within the specified section context, maintaining proper database relationships between articles and sections. The system supports soft deletion through the deleted_at field, allowing content to be archived rather than permanently removed when managing inappropriate content.

Article creation is subject to platform content quality standards and rate limiting policies. Users are limited to creating articles based on configured rate limits to prevent spam and ensure content quality. The system performs comprehensive validation including section existence verification, title/content length requirements, and user permission checks for the selected section.

Upon successful creation, the article becomes immediately visible in the designated section's article list. The response includes the complete article record with server-generated metadata, allowing the client to display the newly created article without requiring additional API calls. Related operations include editing articles via PUT /sections/{sectionCode}/articles/{articleId} and browsing articles through PATCH /sections/{sectionCode}/articles for search and filtering.

The operation integrates with section management system to ensure articles are always associated with valid, active sections. Administrator capabilities allow for article moderation including soft deletion of inappropriate content regardless of authorship.
operations.specification: Validate request body fields: title (5-200 chars), content (min 50 chars), section_id exists and is active. Check user rate limit (10 articles/hour). Verify user has permission to post in the selected section. Create article record with server-generated fields: id (UUID), created_at, updated_at (current timestamp), status 'published'. Set discussion_board_user_id from authenticated user context. Return complete article object with all fields including relationships.

requestBody.description: Article creation data including title, content, and section assignment

responseBody.description: Complete article record with server-generated metadata

operations.specification:
Delete an article by ID with proper authorization checks.

First validate that the article exists and is not already deleted (deleted_at is null).

Authorization logic:
- If the authenticated user is the article author: allow deletion
- If the authenticated user is an administrator (regular or super): allow deletion
- Otherwise: return authorization error

Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp.

Cascade delete all related entities:
- Delete all article files (discussion_board_article_files) with cascade
- Delete all article images (discussion_board_article_images) with cascade  
- Delete all comments (discussion_board_comments) with cascade
- Delete all comment attachments (discussion_board_comment_attachments) through cascade

Return the deleted article information for confirmation.

Handle edge cases:
- Article not found: return 404
- Article already deleted: return 410 Gone
- Unauthorized access: return 403
operations.description:
Mark an article as deleted in the discussion board platform while preserving the record for audit purposes.

This operation allows authenticated users to delete their own articles or administrators to delete any article regardless of ownership. The deletion follows a soft delete pattern where the article record is preserved in the database with a deletion timestamp, but becomes invisible in public interfaces.

When an article is soft-deleted, all associated content including comments, file attachments, and image attachments remains intact but becomes hidden from regular user views. The article's title and content are preserved for moderation and audit trail purposes.

Authorization is strictly enforced - regular users can only delete articles they authored, while administrators have the privilege to delete any article for moderation purposes. The system maintains referential integrity while preserving historical data through the soft delete mechanism.

This operation performs a hard delete of the specified article, completely removing the article record and all related data including comments, file attachments, and image attachments from the database. The deletion is not reversible and affects all associated child records through cascading deletion constraints.

Regular users can only delete articles they authored, while administrators have privileges to delete any article for moderation purposes. The system validates the requesting user's authorization level before proceeding with the deletion operation.

After successful deletion, the operation returns the deleted article information for confirmation. The response includes the article details that were removed from the system.

**Database Impact**: This operation triggers cascading deletions across multiple related tables including discussion_board_comments, discussion_board_article_files, discussion_board_article_images, and discussion_board_comment_attachments.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to delete

operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
Delete an article by ID with proper authorization checks.

First validate that the article exists and is not already deleted (deleted_at is null).

Authorization logic:
- If the authenticated user is the article author: allow deletion
- If the authenticated user is an administrator (regular or super): allow deletion
- Otherwise: return authorization error

Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp.

Cascade delete all related entities:
- Delete all article files (discussion_board_article_files) with cascade
- Delete all article images (discussion_board_article_images) with cascade  
- Delete all comments (discussion_board_comments) with cascade
- Delete all comment attachments (discussion_board_comment_attachments) through cascade

Return the deleted article information for confirmation.

Handle edge cases:
- Article not found: return 404
- Article already deleted: return 410 Gone
- Unauthorized access: return 403

The soft delete mechanism ensures compliance with data retention policies while providing users with draft lifecycle management capabilities. Drafts marked as deleted remain in the system according to the recovery data retention period defined in the discussion_board_article_drafts schema.

The soft deletion process references the draft_deleted_at field in the discussion_board_article_drafts table schema, which stores the timestamp of deletion while maintaining referential integrity with related entities. Soft-deleted drafts remain accessible through specialized administrative interfaces for review or restoration but are excluded from regular user-facing queries and interfaces. This approach balances data retention requirements with content management efficiency.

Related API operations include retrieving soft-deleted drafts through administrative search endpoints and restoring deleted drafts when appropriate. Users should note that this soft deletion differs from hard deletion, where records would be permanently removed from the database. The draft's auto-save and recovery data may be preserved or archived according to system configuration even after soft deletion.

This operation deletes the tag association between an article and a specific tag, effectively removing that tag from the article's tag list. The deletion is permanent and cannot be undone, requiring careful consideration before execution.

This operation is typically used when users want to remove incorrect or outdated tags from their articles, or when administrators need to clean up tag associations for content moderation purposes.

Return appropriate HTTP status codes: 204 No Content on successful deletion, 404 Not Found if the tag association doesn't exist, or 400 Bad Request for invalid parameters.

This operation allows authenticated users to add or remove an极速赛车开奖直播 article from their favorites list. When called, it checks if the article is already favorited by the current user. If not favorited, it creates a new favorite record. If already favorited, it removes the existing favorite record.

The operation validates that the target article exists and is accessible to the user. It returns the current favorite status after the operation completes, allowing the client to immediately update the UI state. This toggle pattern provides a clean, intuitive interface for managing user favorites without requiring separate add/remove endpoints.

Security considerations include ensuring only authenticated users can modify their own favorites and that the target article is valid and accessible. The operation integrates with the discussion_board_article_favorites table which maintains the many-to-many relationship between users and favorited articles.极速赛车开奖直播

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId} to view article details and PATCH /favorites to list all favorited articles. The operation follows the platform's security model where users can only manage their own favorites.
operations.specification: Implement article favorite toggle functionality. First authenticate the user from the session. Validate that the article exists and is accessible (not deleted, published status). Check if a favorite record already exists for this user-article pair in discussion_board_article_favorites table using the composite unique constraint. If favorite exists, delete the record and return favorite status as false. If favorite doesn't exist, create a new record with current timestamp and return favorite status as true. Handle concurrency by using database transactions for the check-create/delete operations. Return appropriate error responses for invalid article ID, unauthorized access, or database errors.

operations.description:
Remove a user's favorite bookmark from a specific article.

This API operation allows authenticated users to remove an article from their favorites list. When a user unfavorites an article, the corresponding record is permanently deleted from the discussion_board_article_favorites junction table. This operation requires the user to be authenticated so the system can identify which user's favorite relationship to remove.

The operation performs a hard deletion of the favorite record, permanently removing the bookmark association between the user and the article. This action is irreversible and immediately updates the user's favorites list. The system validates that the favorite relationship exists before attempting deletion to prevent errors.

Security considerations include ensuring that users can only remove their own favorites, not those of other users. The operation requires valid authentication credentials and proper authorization checks to prevent unauthorized access to favorite management functionality.

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId}/favorites to check if an article is favorited, and POST /articles/{articleId}/favorites to add an article to favorites. These operations work together to provide complete favorite management capabilities for users.
operations.specification:
Authenticate the requesting user from the JWT token to identify the user ID.
Query the discussion_board_article_favorites table to find the record matching both the authenticated user ID and the provided articleId.
If no matching favorite record exists, return a 404 Not Found error.
If the favorite record exists, perform a hard delete operation to remove the record permanently.
Return a 204 No Content response upon successful deletion.
Log the unfavorite action for analytics and user activity tracking.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to remove from favorites
parameters.name: articleId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of article snapshots showing the edit history and version changes for a specific article.

This operation provides access to the complete audit trail of article modifications, allowing users to track how content has evolved over time. Each snapshot represents a point-in-time state of the article, capturing key database fields: title, content, discussion_board_section_id, discussion_board_user_id, and created_at as specified in the discussion_board_article_snapshots schema. Each snapshot records the article's state at the moment of modification, including section assignment and author information.

The response includes snapshot summaries with creation timestamps and basic information, enabling users to compare versions and understand the article's editing history. Pagination ensures efficient loading even for articles with extensive edit histories.

Administrators and article authors typically use this endpoint for content moderation, compliance tracking, and understanding the evolution of discussion board content. The snapshots support rollback capabilities and provide transparency about content changes.

Related API operations: PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId} to retrieve the current article state, and PATCH /discussionBoard/articles for browsing article lists.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific article snapshot by its unique identifier within the context of a parent article.

This operation provides access to historical versions of articles through the snapshot system. Each snapshot represents a point-in-time capture of an article's state, including its title, content, section assignment, and author information at the moment the snapshot was created. The snapshot system supports audit trails, content moderation tracking, and version comparison capabilities.

Security considerations require that users have appropriate permissions to access both the parent article and the specific snapshot. The operation validates that the snapshot belongs to the specified article by checking the discussion_board_article_id foreign key relationship. Snapshots are read-only records that cannot be modified, providing an immutable audit trail of article changes.

Related operations include retrieving the current version of an article through GET /articles/{articleId} and listing all snapshots for an article through GET /articles/{articleId}/snapshots. This operation is particularly useful for content moderation, auditing, and version comparison workflows.

Return the complete snapshot data including title, content, section assignment, author information, and creation timestamp. Ensure that the operation returns a 404 error if either the article or snapshot does not exist, or if the snapshot does not belong to the specified article.

This operation provides comprehensive search functionality for article drafts including status-based filtering, text search across draft titles and content using PostgreSQL full-text search, and date range queries. Users can efficiently browse their draft collection, filter by publication status (draft, published, archived), and search for specific content using advanced search capabilities that leverage the database's gin_trgm_ops indexes for optimal performance.

The operation integrates with the draft management workflow documented in the article requirements, supporting the complete article creation lifecycle from initial draft to final publication as outlined in the system requirements.

This operation allows users to check their voting status on any comment in the discussion board. The system queries the discussion_board_comment_votes table to find the vote record matching both the current user's ID and the specified comment ID. If the user has voted on this comment, the operation returns the vote type (upvote or downvote) along with creation and update timestamps.

Users must be authenticated to access this endpoint as it requires identifying the current user. The operation is particularly useful for frontend applications that need to display the user's current voting status on comments, such as highlighting upvoted/downvoted comments or showing vote counts.

If the user has not voted on the specified comment, the operation returns a null response body. This design allows clients to distinguish between 'no vote' and 'error' scenarios cleanly. The operation respects the unique constraint on user-comment pairs in the database schema.

This operation allows super administrators to promote regular administrators to super administrator status or demote other super administrators to regular administrator. The operation enforces the administrator hierarchy system by validating that only super administrators can perform grade changes and preventing self-demotion for security reasons.

Security validation ensures the requesting administrator is a super administrator and not attempting to demote themselves. The operation creates a detailed audit trail in the discussion_board_administrator_grade_changes table, recording the previous grade, new grade, reason for change, and the administrator who performed the action. This maintains full transparency and accountability in administrator management operations.

The response includes the updated administrator record with the new grade level and timestamps reflecting the change. Related authentication records in discussion_board_admins and discussion_board_super_admins tables are updated accordingly to reflect the new privilege level. The operation supports the platform's governance model where administrator privileges are carefully managed and tracked.

Verify the current grade of the target administrator and validate the requested grade transition is valid (regular→super or super→regular).

Update the administrator's grade in the discussion_board_administrators table, set the grade_changed_at timestamp, and update the appropriate authentication table reference (admin_id or super_admin_id). Create an audit trail record in discussion_board_administrator_grade_changes with the previous grade, new grade, change reason, and performing administrator. Handle edge cases where the administrator doesn't exist, the grade change is invalid, or authorization fails.

Return the updated administrator record with the new grade level and updated timestamps. Ensure all database operations are performed within a transaction to maintain data consistency across the administrator record and audit trail tables.

Workflow status changes are logged with timestamps and reviewer information, providing complete transparency for the administrator promotion process.

This operation is part of the comprehensive administrator management system that maintains platform governance and ensures proper oversight of administrator privileges. operations.description:
Soft delete a system configuration by setting its deleted_at timestamp.

This operation marks a system configuration as deleted by setting the deleted_at field to the current timestamp, effectively removing the configuration from active use while preserving the record for audit and historical purposes. The configuration will no longer be returned in standard queries but can be recovered if needed.

Soft deletion is preferred over hard deletion for system configurations to maintain audit trails and allow configuration recovery in case of accidental deletion. The operation ensures that configuration history is preserved while making the configuration inactive.

Administrators with appropriate permissions can perform this operation to remove outdated or unnecessary system configurations. The operation is idempotent - calling it multiple times on the same configuration will have the same effect as calling it once.

This operation complements the configuration management workflow, allowing administrators to manage the lifecycle of system settings while maintaining data integrity and audit compliance.

operations.specification:
Create a new backup operation record in the system.

## Authentication & Authorization
- Requires administrator authentication
- Validate that the requesting user has administrator privileges
- Capture the authenticated administrator's ID as the initiator

## Business Logic
- Generate a unique UUID for the backup record
- Set default status to 'in_progress' if not specified
- Validate backup_type against allowed values (full, incremental, database_only, files_only)
- Set started_at timestamp to current time
- Initialize completed_at as null
- Validate file_path format if provided
- Ensure size_bytes is only set for completed backups

## Validation Rules
- backup_type: required, must be one of predefined values
- status: defaults to 'in_progress', must be valid status
- file_path: optional, must be valid path format if provided
- size_bytes: only allowed when status is 'completed'
- error_message: only allowed when status is 'failed'

## Database Operations
- Insert new record into discussion_board_backup_records table
- Include all provided fields with system-generated values
- Return the complete new record including system-generated fields

## Error Handling
- Return 401 if user is not authenticated as administrator
- Return 403 if authenticated user does not have admin privileges
- Return 400 for validation errors in request data
- Return 500 for database or system errors

This endpoint provides specialized sorting functionality that prioritizes articles based on their most recent comment activity, rather than just publication date. The operation analyzes comment timestamps across all articles to identify the most recently active discussions, making it ideal for users who want to participate in ongoing conversations.

The system queries both the discussion_board_articles table and the discussion_board_comments table to determine activity patterns. Articles without comments are ranked by their original publication date. Security considerations ensure that only published articles are included in results, respecting content workflow states. The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and cursor-based navigation for efficient browsing of large result sets.

operations.specification:
Query the discussion_board_articles table joined with discussion_board_comments to determine recent activity.

Implementation steps:
1. Join articles with comments on discussion_board_article_id
2. Group by article and select max(comments.created_at) as last_activity
3. For articles without comments, use articles.created_at as last_activity
4. Sort by last_activity descending
5. Apply pagination parameters from request body
6. Filter to only include articles with status = 'published'
7. Return paginated results with summary information

Include article title, author info, section info, comment count, and last_activity timestamp in response. Handle edge cases where articles have no comments or are in draft/archived status.

Performance considerations:
- Use composite indexes on (discussion_board_article_id, created_at) in comments table
- Cache frequently accessed results for performance
- Implement efficient cursor-based pagination

Administrators can approve appeals to overturn bans or reject appeals to uphold bans, providing detailed reasons for their decisions in the `decision_reason` field.

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive system overview statistics and platform metrics for the discussion board platform.

This API operation provides administrators and super administrators with a holistic view of platform health, usage patterns, and system performance. The overview includes aggregated statistics across all major platform entities including user accounts, articles, comments, sections, and administrative activities.

The system overview serves as a dashboard endpoint that enables administrators to monitor platform usage, identify trends, and assess system performance. It provides real-time metrics that help administrators make informed decisions about content management, user engagement, and platform optimization.

Key metrics include total user registrations, active article counts, comment engagement statistics, section utilization rates, and recent system activity patterns. This information is essential for platform administration, capacity planning, and performance monitoring.

Security considerations require that only authenticated administrators and super administrators can access this endpoint, as it contains sensitive system statistics and usage patterns that should not be exposed to regular users.

The operation queries multiple database tables including discussion_board_users, discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_comments, discussion_board_sections, discussion_board_system_activities, and administrator tables to provide comprehensive system metrics. All statistics are calculated in real-time to ensure accuracy and timeliness of the overview data.
operations.specification:
Query multiple database tables to aggregate system statistics and platform metrics.

Execute the following queries:
1. Count total users from discussion_board_users where deleted_at is null
2. Count total articles from discussion_board_articles where deleted_at is null
3. Count total comments from discussion_board_comments where deleted_at is null
4. Count total sections from discussion_board_sections where deleted_at is null
5. Count total administrators from discussion_board_admins where deleted_at is null
6. Count total super administrators from discussion_board_super_admins where deleted_at is null
7. Calculate recent activity counts from discussion_board_system_activities for the last 24 hours
8. Calculate platform uptime based on the earliest created_at timestamp from system configurations

Use database transactions to ensure data consistency across multiple queries. Handle edge cases where tables might be empty or counts might be zero. Return comprehensive error handling for database connection issues.

Performance optimization: Consider using database views or materialized views for frequently accessed statistics if performance becomes an issue. Cache the results for short periods (e.g., 5 minutes) to reduce database load while maintaining data freshness.

Security: Ensure the operation validates administrator authentication and authorization before executing any queries. Log the access to this endpoint for audit trail purposes.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

IDiscussionBoardUserPasswordReset.IReque.description:
Search criteria for filtering password reset records with comprehensive query capabilities.

This request DTO allows administrators to search password reset token records using various filtering options. Search parameters include user email address pattern matching, token usage status (used/unused), expiration status (active/expired), and date range filters for creation and expiration times. All parameters are optional to enable flexible query combinations.

The search supports pagination with configurable page size and cursor-based navigation. Results are filtered to exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL) and include appropriate access controls for administrative review.
IDiscussionBoardUserPasswordReset.IReque.x-autobe-specification: Search implementation: JOIN discussion_board_users ON discussion_board_user_password_resets.discussion_board_user_id = discussion_board_users.id. Filter by email using LIKE pattern matching. Filter by token status: used_at IS NULL for unused tokens, used_at IS NOT NULL for used tokens. Filter by expiration: expired_at < now() for expired tokens, expired_at >= now() for active tokens. Date range filters apply BETWEEN logic on created_at and expired_at fields.

IDiscussionBoardArticleViewStatEvent.IRe.description: Request body for filtering article view analytics data. Supports date range filtering, section-based filtering, user type differentiation, and pagination controls for analytics results. Used by administrators to retrieve comprehensive view statistics and engagement metrics across the discussion board platform.
IDiscussionBoardArticleViewStatEvent.IRe.x-autobe-specification: Analytics filtering criteria for querying article view statistics across the discussion board platform. Implementation should JOIN discussion_board_article_view_stats with discussion_board_articles and discussion_board_sections tables for comprehensive filtering. Apply date range filtering on view statistics timestamps, section filtering via article-section relationships, and user type filtering based on article authorship. Pagination uses OFFSET/LIMIT based on page and limit parameters for efficient data retrieval.
